Based on the search results, here's what I found about ALFWorld on Hugging Face:

## ALFWorld on Hugging Face

ALFWorld builds on TextWorld and ties to the embodied ALFRED benchmark. The dataset is a redistribution of the original ALFWorld data for research convenience.

There are several ALFWorld-related datasets available on the Hugging Face platform:

1. **awawa-agi/alfworld-raw** - A redistribution of the original ALFWorld data provided as-is for academic and research purposes only.

2. **hkust-nlp/agentboard** - Contains 134 rows of alfworld evaluation data.

3. **SFT Trajectory Datasets** - Multiple versions (v3, v4, v5) are available for agent training. These are synthetic SFT (Supervised Fine-Tuning) datasets designed for agent training in ALFWorld-compatible environments. The datasets programmatically generate expert trajectories without requiring an actual ALFWorld environment or a large language model.

These datasets are used for training and evaluating agents that interact with household environments to solve everyday tasks.

Based on the search results, here's information about the ALFWorld benchmark dataset download and setup:

## Installation

To enable visual modalities, use pip install alfworld[vis]. Without the full extra, it will only install the text version of ALFWorld.

## Data Download

Download PDDL & Game files and pre-trained MaskRCNN detector (will be stored in ~/.cache/alfworld/). This should install Alfworld in your virtual environment and download Alfworld data in ~/.cache/alfworld directory. The data is stored by default in the ~/.cache/alfworld/json_2.1.1 directory.

## Dataset Overview

The ALFWorld dataset contains 3,553 training games, 140 seen and 134 unseen validation games. The categories are pick_and_place, look_at_obj_in_light, pick_clean_then_place, pick_heat_then_place, pick_cool_then_place and pick_two_obj_and_place.

## Requirements

See requirements.txt for the prerequisites to run ALFWorld text-only version. See requirements-vis.txt for the prerequisites to run ALFWorld with both text and visual modalities. See requirements-full.txt for the full prerequisites to run experiments.

## Alternative Source

There is also a Hugging Face dataset redistribution containing 3,827 rows with a total file size of 61.5 MB.

The official ALFWorld GitHub repository (https://github.com/alfworld/alfworld) contains the complete setup instructions and documentation.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the WebShop benchmark dataset:

## WebShop Benchmark Dataset Overview

WebShop is a simulated e-commerce website environment with 1.18 million real-world products and 12,087 crowd-sourced text instructions. In this environment, an agent needs to navigate multiple types of webpages and issue diverse actions to find, customize, and purchase a product given an instruction.

## Key Characteristics

WebShop provides several challenges including understanding compositional instructions, query (re-)formulation, dealing with noisy text in webpages, and performing strategic exploration.

## Performance Metrics

The best model achieves a task success rate of 29%, which significantly outperforms rule heuristics but is far lower than expert human performance (59%). Additionally, agents trained on WebShop exhibit non-trivial sim-to-real transfer when evaluated on amazon.com and ebay.com, indicating the potential value of the benchmark for developing practical web agents that can operate in the wild.

## Original Publication

The WebShop benchmark was originally published as a research paper in 2022 and has since become an important benchmark in the field of web-based AI agents for evaluating language grounding and e-commerce task completion.

Based on my search results, here's information about the ScienceWorld benchmark dataset:

## Overview

ScienceWorld is a benchmark to test agents' scientific reasoning abilities in a new interactive text environment at the level of a standard elementary school science curriculum.

## How to Access and Download

ScienceWorld is a text-based virtual environment centered around accomplishing tasks from the standardized elementary science curriculum, and you can try ScienceWorld yourself via our HuggingFace Space or read some of the playthrough transcripts.

The primary repository is available on GitHub, where you can install it via pip using `pip install scienceworld[webserver]`. A Python API is provided (Python >= 3.8), which interfaces using the py4j package.

## Key Features

ScienceWorld consists of a richly parameterized text environment simulating ten interconnected locations (e.g., kitchen, workshop), each populated with up to 200 types of objects. The available action space comprises 25 high-level commands, generating up to 200,000 legal action–object pairs per step. Agents interact with these environments by issuing text commands (e.g., "move to the kitchen," "connect wire to battery"), resulting in changes to the world state and observations returned as textual descriptions.

For more details and to access the benchmark, you can visit the official GitHub repository at https://github.com/allenai/ScienceWorld or try the interactive demo via the HuggingFace Space.

## GPU Hours & Training Time

A GRPO training process for a reasoning model can complete in approximately 27 hours on only eight A100 GPUs, which is useful for research as it allows for quick iteration upon changes to the RL training process.

## Cost for 7B Model Training (General)

Medium models (7B parameters) cost $50K-500K to train from scratch, requiring 2-4 weeks on 64x A100 GPUs. However, this is for standard pretraining rather than GRPO-specific reinforcement learning.

## Memory Requirements for GRPO

GRPO is not just a LoRA job with a different loss function—it consumes 2-3x the VRAM of supervised fine-tuning and requires a rollout generation pipeline.

With 15GB VRAM, platforms like Unsloth allow you to transform any model up to 17B parameters like Llama 3.1 (8B), Phi-4 (14B), Mistral (7B) or Qwen2.5 (7B) into a reasoning model.

## Fine-tuning Cost (GRPO Alternative)

Fine-tuning a 7B model costs $500-5K using LoRA adapters versus $50K-500K for training from scratch.

The exact cost depends heavily on whether you're training from scratch or fine-tuning an existing model, the specific hardware used, and whether you leverage parameter-efficient techniques like LoRA.

Based on the web search results, here's what I found about verl GRPO training and OpenRLHF:

## verl Framework

verl is the open-source version of HybridFlow: A Flexible and Efficient RLHF Framework paper. It enables building RL dataflows such as GRPO, PPO in a few lines of code. The framework supports reinforcement learning with PPO, GRPO, GSPO, ReMax, REINFORCE++, RLOO, PRIME, DAPO, DrGRPO, KL_Cov & Clip_Cov and other algorithms.

verl provides seamless integration of existing LLM infra with modular APIs, enabling integration with existing LLM frameworks, such as FSDP, Megatron-LM, vLLM, SGLang, etc.

## OpenRLHF Framework

OpenRLHF implements PPO, REINFORCE++, REINFORCE++-baseline, GRPO, RLOO with advanced optimization tricks inspired by practical guides and community best practices. OpenRLHF leverages Ray for distributed scheduling, integrates vLLM to achieve efficient response rollout with low GPU memory usage, and employs DeepSpeed ZeRO for 3D parallelism to enable efficient training.

## Relationship and Comparison

verl is inspired by the design of Nemo-Aligner, Deepspeed-chat and OpenRLHF. verl has a big community and is very actively developed and among the most mature open-source RL libraries for LLMs.

Both frameworks support GRPO training for large language models, with verl focused on performance and scalability while OpenRLHF emphasizes ease of use and distributed scheduling through Ray.

## Overview

ART (Agent Reinforcement Trainer) is an open-source training framework for teaching agentic LLMs to improve performance and reliability through experience. ART provides a convenient wrapper around reinforcement learning techniques like GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization) to dramatically improve model performance while minimizing training costs.

## Training Infrastructure

The server runs independently on any machine with a GPU. It abstracts away the complexity of the inference and training portions of the RL loop while allowing for some custom configuration. Completion requests are routed to the ART server, which runs the model's latest LoRA in vLLM.

## GPU Training Costs

A concrete example of training costs comes from the ART·E project: A model achieved higher accuracy while being faster and cheaper than o3, taking fewer turns to answer questions correctly and hallucinating less frequently, all while being trained on a single H100 GPU for under $80. More specifically, training fit on a single H100 GPU using Runpod via Skypilot, completing in under a day for approximately $80 total cost.

## Training Performance

OpenPipe ART finished training in under 40 minutes per run. PPO with Agent-R1 required 6–8 hours for similar experiments.

## Deployment Options

W&B Training (Serverless RL) is the first publicly available service for flexibly training models with reinforcement learning. It manages your training and inference infrastructure automatically, letting you focus on defining your data, environment and reward function—leading to faster feedback cycles, lower costs, and far less DevOps.

## 1. Agent Benchmark Datasets Accessibility

### ALFWorld
- **Available on HuggingFace**: Yes. Multiple datasets exist:
  - [awawa-agi/alfworld-raw](https://huggingface.co/datasets/awawa-agi/alfworld-raw) -- redistribution of the original data (3,827 rows, 61.5 MB)
  - [hkust-nlp/agentboard](https://huggingface.co/datasets/hkust-nlp/agentboard) -- 134 rows of ALFWorld eval data
  - [u-10bei/sft_alfworld_trajectory_dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/u-10bei/sft_alfworld_trajectory_dataset) (multiple versions v3-v5) -- synthetic SFT trajectory datasets for agent training
- **Official repo**: [github.com/alfworld/alfworld](https://github.com/alfworld/alfworld). Install via `pip install alfworld[vis]`. Data auto-downloads to `~/.cache/alfworld/`. Contains 3,553 training games, 140 seen and 134 unseen validation games across 6 task types.
- **Ease of setup**: Straightforward pip install + automatic data download.

### WebShop
- **Official repo**: [github.com/princeton-nlp/WebShop](https://github.com/princeton-nlp/WebShop) (Princeton NLP, NeurIPS 2022)
- **Dataset**: 1.18 million real-world products, 12,087 crowd-sourced text instructions
- **Setup**: Requires Python 3.8.13, Java, and running `setup.sh` which downloads data via gdown. Options for small (1,000 products) or full dataset. More involved than ALFWorld -- requires a web server and multiple dependencies.
- **HuggingFace**: Paper page exists at [huggingface.co/papers/2207.01206](https://huggingface.co/papers/2207.01206) but no standalone dataset repo found.

### ScienceWorld
- **Official repo**: [github.com/allenai/ScienceWorld](https://github.com/allenai/ScienceWorld) (Allen AI)
- **Install**: `pip install scienceworld[webserver]` (Python >= 3.8, uses py4j)
- **Environment**: Text-based, 10 interconnected locations, up to 200 object types, 25 high-level commands generating up to 200,000 legal action-object pairs per step.
- **Interactive demo**: Available via HuggingFace Spaces at [sciworld.apps.allenai.org](https://sciworld.apps.allenai.org/)
- **Ease of setup**: Simple pip install, straightforward Python API.

**Summary**: All three are publicly available and open-source. ALFWorld and ScienceWorld are easy to set up (pip install). WebShop is more involved (requires Java, web server, data download scripts).

## 2. GPU Cost Estimates for Agent RL Training

### H100 Pricing (2026)
- **On-demand range**: $1.49--$6.98/hr across 15+ providers, averaging ~$3.20/hr ([IntuitionLabs comparison](https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/h100-rental-prices-cloud-comparison))
- **Specific providers**: GMI Cloud $2.00/hr (PCIe), $2.40/hr (SXM); Jarvislabs $2.69/hr; Baseten up to $9.98/hr
- **1-year contract**: ~$2.35/hr/GPU as of March 2026 (up ~40% from $1.70 low in Oct 2025)
- **Trend**: On-demand prices up ~9% since May 2025 ($3.35 to $3.65/hr)

### A100 Pricing (2026)
- **On-demand range**: $0.13--$5.04/hr depending on provider
- **Specific providers**: Hyperstack A100 80GB at $1.35/hr; Jarvislabs at $1.49/hr; decentralized platforms $0.96--$1.29/hr
- **Trend**: Down ~17% since May 2025 ($2.39 to $1.98/hr average)

### Cost to Train 7B Model with GRPO (~80-200 H100 hours)
Based on the data gathered:
- **Single H100 GRPO LoRA fine-tune**: 8-12 hours = **$10--$16** (QLoRA approach via Unsloth)
- **8x A100 GRPO training run**: ~27 hours = roughly **$320--$430** (at ~$1.50--$2.00/hr per GPU)
- **8x H100 full fine-tune**: 24-48 hours = **$250--$510**
- **OpenPipe ART concrete example**: Single H100, under 1 day, total cost approximately **$80** for a complete GRPO agent training run
- **At 80-200 H100 GPU-hours at $2-3.50/hr**: That's **$160--$700** total cost

The key insight: GRPO is more memory-efficient than PPO (no separate reward/value model), so costs are lower than traditional RLHF. With LoRA/QLoRA, a 7B GRPO run on agent tasks can be done for **well under $500** on cloud GPUs.

## 3. GRPO Training Frameworks for Agents

### Major Frameworks

1. **[OpenPipe/ART](https://github.com/OpenPipe/ART)** (Agent Reinforcement Trainer)
   - Purpose-built for multi-step agent GRPO training
   - Supports Qwen 2.5, Qwen 3, Llama, and more
   - Training completes in ~40 minutes per run; ~$80 total on a single H100
   - Integrated into [NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit](https://docs.nvidia.com/nemo/agent-toolkit/latest/improve-workflows/finetuning/rl_with_openpipe.html)

2. **[verl (HybridFlow)](https://github.com/verl-project/verl)**
   - Supports GRPO, PPO, GSPO, ReMax, REINFORCE++, RLOO, PRIME, DAPO, DrGRPO
   - Integrates with FSDP, Megatron-LM, vLLM, SGLang
   - Very active community, among the most mature RL-for-LLM libraries

3. **[verl-agent](https://github.com/langfengq/verl-agent)** (extension of verl)
   - Specifically designed for training LLM/VLM agents via RL
   - Supports 7B models on just 2 H100 GPUs
   - Implements GRPO, PPO, DAPO, GSPO, RLOO, and GiGPO (new SOTA algorithm)

4. **[OpenRLHF](https://github.com/openrlhf/openrlhf)**
   - Implements PPO, REINFORCE++, GRPO, RLOO
   - Uses Ray for distributed scheduling + vLLM for rollouts + DeepSpeed ZeRO
   - Emphasizes ease of use and scalability

5. **[AMAP-ML/Tree-GRPO](https://github.com/AMAP-ML/Tree-GRPO)** (ICLR 2026)
   - Tree-search rollout strategy instead of independent chain-based rollouts
   - Reduces rollout budget via tree-based process supervision

6. **[lsdefine/simple_GRPO](https://github.com/lsdefine/simple_GRPO)**
   - Minimal implementation (~200 lines of code, 2 files)
   - Only depends on deepspeed + torch; trains 7B on single 80G A800

7. **[Unsloth](https://unsloth.ai/docs/get-started/reinforcement-learning-rl-guide)**
   - GRPO training on as little as 5GB VRAM
   - Supports models up to 17B parameters

---

## 4. ALFWorld and WebShop SOTA Results (2025-2026)

### ALFWorld SOTA

| Method | Success Rate | Notes |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| **Embodied Planner-R1** | **97.78%** | Current best; only -3.66% drop on unseen environments |
| AgentPRM / InversePRM | 88--91% | Compact 3B models, exceeds GPT-based prompting baselines |
| SKILL0 | 87.9% | +9.7% over AgentOCR; 5x context token cost reduction |
| GRPO (baseline, 7B) | 53.5--76.7% | Degrades on longer horizons (76.7% short to 53.5% long) |
| GRPO + Mem0 | 54.7% | Slight improvement over vanilla GRPO |
| Tree-GRPO (MCTS) | 39.48% | From 11.57% initial, over 30 training iterations |
| ReSpAct | ReAct + 6% absolute | Reduces invalid actions from 13% to 3% |

### WebShop SOTA
- **Original paper baseline** (2022): Best model 29% success rate vs. 59% human expert
- **GPT-4 agent** (2024): ~14% success rate initially
- Specific recent SOTA numbers for WebShop are harder to find, as the community has shifted focus to newer benchmarks like **WebArena** and **WebVoyager**. WebShop is still used but less actively benchmarked by frontier labs.

### ScienceWorld SOTA
- **Leading models** (early 2025): Scores in the **low 80s** (dramatic improvement from sub-10% three years prior)
- **Embodied Planner-R1**: **79.92%** on ScienceWorld
- **KnowMap + GPT-4-Turbo**: 17.71% improvement over base GPT-4-Turbo
- Still far from fully solving elementary science curriculum tasks
